activities.title: Exact Match (EM) and Token-Level Precision, Recall, and F1

source_resources.title: Hugging Face LLM Evaluation Guidebook (legacy edition)
source_resources.author: Hugging Face evaluation-guidebook contributors
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: Public edition checked 2026-11-01; moving pages may change
source_resources.permission_basis: External hyperlink only; no third-party prose, exercises, code or translations are imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Held-out data, basic language-model metrics and experimental comparisons.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Teaching-oriented evaluation design and reproducibility guidance complements the benchmark papers. Stable methodological chapters only; not a current tooling/version reference.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: README says no longer maintained. The replacement OpenEvals Space was not verified as containing the guidebook; its license and content are not substituted. No bootstrap derivation is claimed.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Use the original localized explanations, exercises and checks already present in this activity; no external account or purchase is required for that fallback.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Retained for the multi-metric framework; the guidebook makes practical choices easier to teach.
Useful implementation cross-check; tool configuration alone does not teach metric choice or evaluator limitations.

source_resources.title: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text
source_resources.author: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of evaluation standard definition.
source_resources.prerequisites: Tokenization, text normalization, precision, recall, and harmonic mean F1.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Defines the standard NLP Exact Match (EM) and token-level Macro/Micro F1 evaluation metrics, establishing standard text normalization rules (lowercasing, punctuation stripping, article removal).
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv and Stanford NLP.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Exact normalization code, multiset token intersection logic, and F1 calculations are completely coded in lesson exercises.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Rajpurkar et al. Know What You Don't Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD 2.0
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Adds unanswerable questions; SQuAD 1.1 formalizes the foundational token F1 and EM mathematical definitions.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Reddy et al. CoQA: A Conversational Question Answering Challenge
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Conversational multi-turn QA; SQuAD provides a widely adopted implementation of normalized token F1.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 6.1 Model Evaluation (Exact match and macro-averaged F1)

source_resources.title: BLEU: a Method for Automatic Evaluation of Machine Translation
source_resources.author: Kishore Papineni, Salim Roukos, Todd Ward, Wei-Jing Zhu
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of foundational n-gram precision metric.
source_resources.prerequisites: N-gram precision, modified n-gram clipping, brevity penalty.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational literature introducing modified n-gram precision and brevity penalties, providing the mathematical contrast between precision-oriented n-gram clipping and recall-oriented sequence metrics.
source_resources.safe_fallback: N-gram clipping algorithms, geometric mean precision, and brevity penalty formulas are completely implemented in lesson code.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Banerjee & Lavie. METEOR: An Automatic Metric for MT Evaluation with Improved Correlation with Human Judgments
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Incorporates stemming and WordNet synonymy; BLEU is the fundamental n-gram precision baseline required for quantitative comparison.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Popović. chrF: character n-gram F-score for automatic MT evaluation
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Character-level n-gram F-score; Papineni BLEU provides the historic foundation for token-based precision clipping.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 2.1.1 Modified n-gram precision on blocks of text; Section 2.3 BLEU details

activities.title: Sequence Overlap Metrics: ROUGE-L and Longest Common Subsequence

source_resources.title: ROUGE: A Package for Automatic Evaluation of Summaries
source_resources.author: Chin-Yew Lin
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of sequence evaluation literature.
source_resources.prerequisites: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS), dynamic programming, recall-oriented evaluation.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary literature establishing ROUGE-N and ROUGE-L (Longest Common Subsequence), deriving sequence-level recall, precision, and F-measure without requiring consecutive n-gram matches.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Dynamic programming LCS algorithms and ROUGE-L scoring equations are completely self-contained in lesson code.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Zhang et al. BERTScore: Evaluating Text Generation with BERT
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Embedding similarity based metric; ROUGE-L provides exact deterministic surface-form sequence overlap without model weights.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Zhao et al. MoverScore: Text Generation Evaluating with Contextualized Embeddings and Earth Mover Distance
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Optimal transport metric; ROUGE-L is the required universal baseline for summary and instruction evaluation.

source_resources.title: A Call for Clarity in Reporting BLEU Scores
source_resources.author: Matt Post
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of evaluation reproducibility standards.
source_resources.prerequisites: Tokenization standardization, evaluation parameters, string normalization pipelines.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Critical paper on metric reproducibility, proving how inconsistent tokenization schemes and smoothing parameters alter reported metrics by multiple percentage points, demanding standardized evaluation strings.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Standardized token normalization pipelines, deterministic tokenizer flags, and signature strings are implemented in curriculum exercises.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Specific ROUGE implementation; Post et al. provides the overarching reproducibility doctrine for NLP metric reporting.
Unified evaluation framework; Post establishes the critical methodology for eliminating hidden tokenization divergence.

activities.title: Held-Out Log-Likelihood Evaluation & Perplexity Under Length Penalties

source_resources.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
source_resources.author: Alec Radford, Jeffrey Wu, Rewon Child, David Luan, Dario Amodei, Ilya Sutskever
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of foundation language model research.
source_resources.prerequisites: Autoregressive conditional likelihood, cross-entropy loss, perplexity exponentiation.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational demonstration of zero-shot task transfer via log-likelihood evaluation over target candidate completions, formalizing length normalization and held-out perplexity scoring.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Conditional log-likelihood equations, length normalization factors, and held-out cross-entropy calculations are fully derived in lesson material.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Kaplan et al. Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Focuses on empirical power-law loss curves; Radford et al. establishes the zero-shot log-likelihood task evaluation protocol.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Hoffmann et al. Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Optimal compute scaling; Radford provides the fundamental zero-shot conditional probability formulation.

source_resources.title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
source_resources.author: Ari Holtzman, Jan Buys, Li Du, Maxwell Forbes, Yejin Choi
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Softmax probabilities, cumulative probability distributions from Days 25-27 and 41-42.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary source introducing Nucleus (Top-p) sampling and analyzing the failure of greedy decoding (loops, repetition).
source_resources.safe_fallback: Top-p truncation algorithms and worked probability cutoffs are completely explained in the lesson.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Fan et al. Hierarchical Neural Story Generation (Top-k)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Introduces top-k sampling; Holtzman et al. dynamic nucleus threshold is compared directly against top-k.
Practical library guide; Holtzman provides the foundational mathematical reasoning.

activities.title: Assessment: Non-Parametric Bootstrap Confidence Intervals on Small Slices

source_resources.title: Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife
source_resources.author: Bradley Efron
source_resources.license: Institute of Mathematical Statistics copyright / Academic linking only
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of foundational statistical resampling methodology.
source_resources.prerequisites: Empirical distributions, sampling with replacement, confidence intervals, standard error.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Original statistical work introducing non-parametric bootstrap resampling, enabling rigorous confidence interval estimation without Gaussian distribution assumptions.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Hosted on Project Euclid; free-access status could not be verified because the site blocks automated access.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Bootstrap resampling algorithms with replacement, empirical percentile confidence interval bounds, and standard error formulas are coded in Python.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Student. The Probable Error of a Mean (Biometrika 1908)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Requires strong normality assumptions; Efron's non-parametric bootstrap applies directly to non-Gaussian NLP accuracy metrics.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Fisher. The Design of Experiments (Permutation Testing 1935)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Tests sharp null hypotheses under exchangeability; bootstrap directly yields confidence intervals for point estimates.

source_resources.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
source_resources.author: Philipp Koehn
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of empirical NLP significance testing.
source_resources.prerequisites: Paired bootstrap resampling, hypothesis testing, p-values, test set variance.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Pioneering application of paired bootstrap resampling in NLP evaluation, demonstrating how to compute statistical significance and prevent false claims of model superiority on small test slices.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Paired bootstrap hypothesis testing, delta confidence intervals, and empirical p-value computation are completely implemented in lesson code.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Dror et al. The Hitchhiker's Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in NLP
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Modern comprehensive survey of significance testing; Koehn 2004 is the established, accessible paired bootstrap paper in NLP.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Berg-Kirkpatrick et al. An Empirical Investigation of Statistical Significance in NLP
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Evaluates optimizer vs test-set randomness; Koehn provides the direct, actionable paired test-set bootstrap.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 5 Bootstrap Resampling and Section 6 Paired Bootstrap Resampling
